:::{#exm-newton-maximum}
#### Newton's method can find a maximum

From $x^{(0)} = -2.5$ the same iteration gives $-2.05$, $-2.000610$, $-2.0000001$, approaching $-2$.
But $-2$ is not a minimizer of $f$:
it is a [stationary point](#def-stationary-point) of $-f$,
whose [second derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-second-derivative) at $-2$ is $-f''(-2) = 4 > 0$,
so it is a strict local minimizer of $-f$ (@thm-second-order-condition),
that is, $f$ is strictly larger at $-2$ than at all nearby points.
Newton's method looks only for a stationary point,
and in this example the [Hessian](vector-calculus.qmd#def-hessian) $H = f''(x) = 2x$ is negative at every [iterate](#def-iterate).
If $H < 0$, then @thm-newton-model does not apply,
because it requires a [positive definite](linear-algebra.qmd#def-positive-definite) Hessian.
Instead, the [model](#def-quadratic-model) $\quadmodelf{\step}$
tends to $-\infty$ as $\abs{\step} \to \infty$,
so it has no minimizer.

@fig-newton-maximum shows the [cubic](algebra.qmd#def-cubic-polynomial) and its model.

{{< include mds/_subfiles/vector-calc/_fig-newton-maximum.qmd >}}

:::
